Declare an analysis before running it

Source: R/prereg.R
prrgdecl.Rd

prrgdecl() records, before the analysis is run, the statistics it intends to report and the claim each one is meant to test, with a UTC timestamp. prrgchk() compares that declaration with what was actually reported and lists the departures in both directions. Seal the declaration with cpsatst() and it acquires a date it cannot be moved off. Use the pair to make a pre-analysis plan checkable.

Usage

prrgdecl(hyps, note = NULL)

prrgchk(prereg, rptd)

Arguments

hyps

Named character vector: one claim per statistic, named by the statistic's name as it will be recorded.

note

Optional character string, default NULL: free text – the design, the data source, what would count as a refutation. Only the first element is kept.

prereg

A declaration from prrgdecl().

rptd

Character vector of the statistic names actually reported, or a manifest (any list with a named results element, such as a capsule manifest), whose result names are used.

Value

prrgdecl() returns a list of class bricklayer_prereg with statistics (the names), hypotheses (the claims), note and decutc (ISO 8601 time).

prrgchk() returns a list of class bricklayer_prereg_check with ok (logical: no departures), the character vectors decnotrep and repnotdec, hypotheses (a data frame of statistic, hypothesis and logical reported) and decutc. Both print a short summary.

Details

The comparison prrgchk() makes is asymmetric on purpose, because the two ways of departing from a plan are different failures:

  • a declared statistic that was NOT reported is outcome switching – the analysis was run and its result dropped;

  • a reported statistic that was NOT declared is an addition, and twenty of them is why a nominal p of 0.05 means nothing.

Neither is misconduct on its own and both are invisible without a declaration made in advance.

Statistics are matched by exact name. The timestamp is the computer's clock at the time of the call, so on its own it proves nothing; the attestation is what fixes the date. Nothing is written to disk.

Errors: hyps not a non-empty character vector with non-empty, unique names; prereg not from prrgdecl().

See also

cpsatst() to seal a declaration, cpsfals() for the controls themselves, falsfam() for the correction that additions make necessary.

Examples

plan <- prrgdecl(c(
  ate = "use of force is higher in the exposed division",
  nrows = "the extract has the row count the source publishes"),
  note = "OTIS 2019-2024, division-level, pre-specified")

# afterwards, against what was reported
prrgchk(plan, c("ate", "nrows"))$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# dropping a declared outcome is outcome switching
prrgchk(plan, "nrows")$decnotrep
#> [1] "ate"

# and adding undeclared ones is what makes a nominal p meaningless
prrgchk(plan, c("ate", "nrows", "atebyyear",
                     "atebyprecinct"))$repnotdec
#> [1] "atebyyear"     "atebyprecinct"

# the full check prints the departures
prrgchk(plan, c("ate", "atebyyear"))
#> ╭── Against the declaration of 2026-10-28T06:50:08Z: departures below ──╮
#> │ ✖ NOT VERIFIED                                                        │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   Declared  2                                                         │
#> │   Reported  1                                                         │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   statistic  reported                                                 │
#> │   ---------  --------                                                 │
#> │   ate        TRUE                                                     │
#> │   nrows      FALSE                                                    │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   The report departs from the declaration: see below.                 │
#> │                                                                       │
#> │   ✖    declared but not reported (outcome switching): nrows           │
#> │   ✖    reported but not declared (1 addition(s)): atebyyear           │
#> ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

try(prrgdecl(c("an unnamed claim")))
#> Error : `hyps` must be a named character vector: one claim per statistic
